title: Event contracts as swaps: the plumbing both outcomes commission
map_limitation: Four blind spots specific to THIS map, and the first one is the reason it is eleven links rather than fifteen. (1) The two firms at the centre of the occurrence do not file: Kalshi and Polymarket are private, and so is every incumbent on the eligibility gate (GeoComply, Xpoint, Jumio, Socure, Persona, Sumsub), the dominant market maker (Susquehanna), the block broker (Cantor Fitzgerald), the state testing labs (GLI, BMM) and the clearing utility on the securities route (OCC). Two of eleven links therefore carry an EMPTY example_tickers list by design and a third carries one ticker, and the money on those links is real. (2) Supplier-side EDGAR full-text search is close to useless here. This is a services chain with no bill of materials: no filer discloses 'we supply geolocation to Kalshi', and the four non-US listings that matter to it (KAMBI.ST, plus the Playtech, Bragg and OpenBet layer this map could not date a source for) file outside the SEC entirely. Everything on this map arrived through dated research, not through fts, which inverts the usual discovery motion. (3) Two stages were checked and NOT built for want of a citable source: a separate market-making technology and matching-engine-vendor stage (the venues either build it or acquire it with the licence, and no listed vendor was cited selling one into this chain), and a state and tribal licensing administration stage distinct from the regulatory gate (GLI and BMM publish standards pages with no publication date, which this map refuses). One edge was also dropped: surveillance-and-integrity into the sportsbook branch is almost certainly real, and no dated source opened this run establishes it, so it is not drawn. (4) The map cannot see how the fee actually splits. Every per-contract economic on it is directional: the Nasdaq surveillance contract, the Sportradar and Genius data deals, the Kambi ten-year Nevada agreement and the ICE stake are all disclosed as relationships with no disclosed price except the ICE equity number, and the one vivid issuer-level figure available tonight (a listed brokerage's quarterly event-contract revenue) was refused under the venue rule rather than carried.

bottleneck.note: Rights are exclusive per competition, so a venue cannot route around the holder of a given league's official feed. Not scored CHOKE_POINT because the layer is contested at the venue level: Kalshi and Polymarket each signed BOTH Sportradar and Genius within three months, which is the behaviour of a buyer with two suppliers, not one.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Two listed issuers hold most of the US betting-data distribution rights, and each holds them per league rather than across the board: Sportradar cited on MLB, NHL, MLS, UFC and Wimbledon, Genius on soccer and its own league book.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low within a competition (the official feed is contractual and exclusive), high across the venue's product set (a venue can list markets on whatever leagues its supplier carries).
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not established on this map. Sportradar and Genius are both listed and both disclose league rights costs, but no figure carried here is issuer-level, by the venue rule.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: SRAD sits on this link AND on market-surveillance-and-integrity (UFDS AI, Integrity Exchange) AND supplies odds into sportsbook-platform-and-trading. A position in SRAD is one bet wearing three link labels on this chain, not three exposures.

links.name: Identity verification, KYC/AML and geolocation gating
links.role: The gate every account passes before it can trade or bet: identity verification and KYC at onboarding, sanctions and AML monitoring, and device-level geolocation deciding which state or country a user is actually in, which is a control that a state gaming licence and a CFTC exchange obligation both demand.

evidence.claim: FanDuel renewed its partnership with GeoComply and will continue relying on its identity verification and fraud prevention tools, with KYC checks, identity verification and enhanced diligence measures used to confirm customer eligibility, under an embedded arrangement covering location and device intelligence across FanDuel's sportsbook, casino and prediction markets products.
evidence.source_name: Bettors Insider, FanDuel and GeoComply renew multi-year partnership for geolocation and compliance technology
source_excerpt: FanDuel will continue relying on GeoComply's identity verification and fraud prevention tools to protect customers and preserve platform integrity.

The combination of KYC checks, identity verification, and enhanced diligence measures helps FanDuel confirm customer eligibility, speed up account registration, reinforce compliance safeguards, and stop fraudulent activity before it happens.

That embedded arrangement is designed to deepen the use of location and device intelligence, behavioral signals, and real-time fraud detection across FanDuel's sportsbook, casino, and prediction markets products.

evidence.claim: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform asked Polymarket and Kalshi for documents on the identity verification technologies, vendors and procedures each platform uses at account creation and at subsequent intervals, on whether international account holders face the same know your customer requirements as US-based users, and on the criteria, thresholds and algorithmic tools each platform uses to flag anomalous trading.
evidence.source_name: ID Tech Wire, House Oversight Asks Polymarket and Kalshi for Identity Verification and KYC Records
source_excerpt: the committee wants documents on the identity verification technologies, vendors, and procedures each platform uses at account creation and at subsequent intervals
whether international account holders face the same know your customer requirements as US-based users, or are routed through reduced-scrutiny pathways by geography or account type
the criteria, thresholds, and algorithmic tools each platform uses to flag anomalous trading, including trades that may reflect the use of nonpublic or classified information

bottleneck.note: Every account on either side of the split passes this gate, and it is the layer Congress asked both exchanges to document. The ticker list is deliberately EMPTY: GeoComply, Xpoint, Jumio, Socure, Persona and Sumsub are all private, and no dated source opened this run ties a listed identity vendor (LexisNexis Risk/RELX, TransUnion, Equifax, Experian, Mitek) to a named prediction-market or sportsbook customer. Naming one would have been a guess.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Not established with a citation this run. GeoComply's own share claims were only reachable through undated vendor pages, which this map refuses.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low at the operator level once integrated (the vendor sits inside registration, fraud scoring and session re-checks), which is what the FanDuel renewal's embedded forward-deployed engineers describe.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Unknowable from public filings: the incumbent is private.

links.name: Market surveillance, trade reporting and betting integrity
links.role: The monitoring layer a regulated venue has to buy: trade-practice surveillance detecting manipulation and insider trading, the pipe that hands trade data to the regulator in the regulator's own format, and the sport-side fraud detection that flags suspicious wagering to leagues and operators.

evidence.claim: Kalshi announced a multi-year partnership with Nasdaq Market Surveillance to enhance monitoring and oversight of trading activity on its markets, on an institutional-grade platform designed to support real-time detection of market abuse, manipulation, insider trading and related misconduct, and to support delivery of Kalshi's trade data to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in the format the agency requires.
evidence.source_name: Kalshi, Kalshi Partners With Nasdaq Market Surveillance
source_excerpt: Kalshi, the next-generation financial exchange, today announced a multi-year partnership with Nasdaq Market Surveillance to enhance monitoring and oversight of trading activity on its markets.
The institutional-grade platform is designed to support real-time detection of market abuse, manipulation, insider trading, and related misconduct.

The platform will also support the delivery of Kalshi's trade data to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), in the format the agency requires, in line with Kalshi's obligations as a CFTC-regulated exchange.

evidence.claim: Kalshi will implement Nasdaq's surveillance technology in phases across its event contracts and perpetual-style futures markets, with cross-market and cross-asset monitoring including real-time detection of potential manipulation, insider trading and other forms of misconduct.
evidence.source_name: Hedgeweek, Kalshi adopts Nasdaq surveillance tech to strengthen market oversight
source_excerpt: The agreement will see Kalshi implement Nasdaq's surveillance technology in phases across its event contracts and perpetual-style futures markets.
The platform will provide cross-market and cross-asset monitoring capabilities, including real-time detection of potential manipulation, insider trading and other forms of misconduct.
The technology will also support Kalshi's submission of trade data to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in the format required by the regulator.

bottleneck.note: Surveillance is not optional for a CFTC-regulated venue and the Kalshi deal is explicitly tied to the exchange's reporting obligation, so the spend arrives with the licence rather than with the volume. HIGH rather than CHOKE_POINT because Nasdaq, Sportradar, Eventus and in-house systems all sell into it.

capture_inputs.substitutability: Medium. Kalshi is combining Nasdaq's platform with its own existing monitoring rather than replacing it, per the phased rollout, so the incumbent vendor is additive not exclusive.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not established here. Nasdaq does not disclose surveillance revenue by customer and no issuer-level figure is carried, by the venue rule.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: SRAD and GENI also sit on official-event-data; their integrity products are sold into the same contracts as their data, so the two links are one commercial relationship for those two issuers.

links.name: Licence, designation and self-certification: permission to list
links.role: The permission layer both outcomes run through and the thing the circuit split is actually about: a state or tribal gaming licence on one side, a CFTC designated-contract-market and clearing registration plus contract self-certification on the other, with no venue on either side able to open without one of them.

evidence.claim: The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court's dissolution of Kalshi's preliminary injunction against Nevada and found Kalshi unlikely to succeed on its claim that the Commodity Exchange Act preempts Nevada's gaming regulations, a decision described as bolstering tribal and state regulators evaluating whether emerging prediction market platforms must comply with existing gaming frameworks before offering sports-related contracts.

unlikely to succeed on its claim that the CEA preempts Nevada's gaming regulations
The regulation of gambling has been and remains a matter for states and Tribes, not an incidental byproduct of federal derivatives oversight

evidence.claim: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued Kalshi Klear LLC an Order of Registration as a derivatives clearing organization.
evidence.source_name: CFTC, CFTC Grants Kalshi Klear LLC DCO Registration (Release 8957-24)
source_excerpt: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has issued Kalshi Klear LLC (Kalshi) an Order of Registration as a derivatives clearing organization (DCO)

bottleneck.note: ARCH-003 in regulatory dress: this link sets whether every downstream link gets commissioned at all, and there is no instrument for it. State gaming boards, tribal regulators and the CFTC issue the permission; the private testing labs that certify to state standards (GLI, BMM) do not file. The empty ticker list is the finding, not an omission.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Total and public. One federal regulator plus roughly fifty state regimes and the tribal compacts; the Ninth Circuit decision moves the boundary between them rather than removing either.
capture_inputs.substitutability: None. This is the only link on the map a venue cannot buy its way around, which is why both regimes commission everything downstream of it.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Nobody investable. The 2025 state take was $18.09 billion of gaming tax, cited on end-user-demand, and it accrues to states.

bottleneck.note: The rails are real and regime-agnostic (the same five methods appear on Kalshi, Polymarket US, DraftKings Predictions and FanDuel Predicts) but they are also substitutable and priced competitively: the deposit fee sits with the user, not the venue.

capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Paysafe is the only issuer here with a cited iGaming-specific disclosure, and even that is segment-level (Digital Wallets, 15% organic growth), not a prediction-market line.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: Circle appears here only because Polymarket's collateral IS USDC; it is the same exposure as the clearing-and-collateral link on the crypto-native venue, not a second one.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: Understated on this map. Playtech, Bragg, OpenBet and Betgenius all sell into this layer and none of them reached a dated source this run, so the two tickers here are a floor, not a census.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low once signed: the Station Casinos contract runs ten years and bundles platform, trading and player accounts, which is a switching cost measured in years.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not established here; no issuer-level figure is carried, by the venue rule.

bottleneck.note: The seat is scarce because the licence is scarce, not because the technology is: five listed issuers reached it by buying or building a designation (ICE via Polymarket, DraftKings via Railbird, IBKR via ForecastEx, CME via FanDuel, Cboe via an options wrapper). The two largest venues by volume, Kalshi and Polymarket, are private, which is the crowdedness trap on this link.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: The listed side is fragmented and each name reached it differently; the unlisted side (Kalshi, Polymarket) holds the volume. ICE paid up to $2 billion for a stake at an $8 billion pre-money valuation rather than build, which is a disclosed price for entry to this link.
capture_inputs.substitutability: Low for the licence, high for the software. DraftKings bought Railbird for its CFTC licence and technology together; Cboe reached the same product through an options wrapper and OCC clearing without a DCM at all, which shows there are two legal routes to one economic seat.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not established here. Every listed name on this link is diversified and none of them breaks out event-contract economics in anything cited on this map.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: ICE, CBOE, CME and IBKR appear again on clearing-and-collateral because in this architecture the venue and the clearing house are usually the same corporate family. Holding two of them is not diversification across the two links.

links.name: Clearing, margin and collateral
links.role: Where the contract actually settles: a registered derivatives clearing organization or the OCC standing between the two sides, holding member funds and margin and paying the winning side at resolution, which is the function that makes an event contract a cleared instrument rather than a bet.

bottleneck.note: Registration is granted one entity at a time by the CFTC (Kalshi Klear) or the product is routed into an existing utility (OCC), so the seat count is set administratively. Not CHOKE_POINT because the two roads, a new DCO or the OCC via an options wrapper, are both open and both have been walked in the last two years.

capture_inputs.supply_concentration: High by construction: clearing is a natural monopoly per venue, and the OCC leg is a single mutualised utility that no listed issuer owns outright.
capture_inputs.substitutability: None once a contract is listed; the clearing house is fixed by the venue's own designation.
capture_inputs.who_posted_the_margin: Not established. Kalshi Klear is inside a private group; the OCC is a utility; and the listed exchanges do not break out event-contract clearing in anything cited here.
capture_inputs.shared_bom: Identical to prediction-market-venue for CME, CBOE, ICE and IBKR. One issuer, two links, one bet.

links.name: Market making and institutional risk transfer
links.role: The firms that quote both sides, without which an event contract has a price and no fill: proprietary trading firms pricing prediction markets around the clock, and the brokers organising block trades on top of them for institutional size.

notes.text: The thesis was tested, not assumed, and it partly survives. The claim on the card is that BOTH regulatory outcomes commission the same plumbing. Of eleven links, seven are regime-agnostic on the evidence: official-event-data (Sportradar and Genius signed sportsbooks first and prediction markets in 2026 on the same product), player-eligibility-gate (one GeoComply contract explicitly spans FanDuel's sportsbook, casino and prediction markets), funding-and-settlement-rails (the same five deposit methods appear on Kalshi, Polymarket US, DraftKings Predictions and FanDuel Predicts), regulatory-gate, distribution-front-ends and end-user-demand, plus market-surveillance-and-integrity where the sport side and the exchange side are the same two vendors. Two links are regime-contingent and are marked as such: sportsbook-platform-and-trading only gets commissioned if the state and tribal regime prevails, and clearing-and-collateral plus liquidity-provision only exist at scale in the federal lane. So the honest version of the card's claim is 'most of the plumbing, not all of it', and the map says which is which.

Archetypes. ARCH-003 (the uninvestable order-book owner) FIRES, inverted: regulatory-gate is this chain's version, the link that decides whether every downstream link gets commissioned at all and that has no instrument. ARCH-007 (a famous layer as a leaf) FIRES on distribution-front-ends, which is where all the coverage went and which repriced the same session. ARCH-002 (volume without capture) is checked and does NOT fire cleanly: funding-and-settlement-rails is the closest shape, high volume and competed pricing, but nobody on it is bidding for a fixed-price contract, so it is recorded as a partial match rather than claimed. ARCH-001, ARCH-004 and ARCH-005 are checked and do NOT fire: there is no precision-manufacturing step, no critical material and no power or grid equipment on a services chain, and their absence is the finding, not a gap to pad. ARCH-006 (geopolitical counter-response as a first-class link) is checked with intent because the log flags it as the corpus's most likely systematic miss, and its analogue here is the reaction of the OTHER regulator: the CFTC's own rulemaking, moving on an independent clock from the courts. It is built into regulatory-gate rather than given its own link, because both forums gate the same permission and splitting them would double-count one topological root. NO new archetype is proposed: a services chain with no physical input is a first for this corpus and one instance is not a pattern.

Shared-link declaration, per the capture_inputs discipline. Three issuers occupy more than one link on this map and a portfolio that held all of them would be less diversified than it looks. SRAD sits on official-event-data, market-surveillance-and-integrity and sportsbook-platform-and-trading: one commercial relationship, three link labels. IBKR sits on prediction-market-venue, clearing-and-collateral and distribution-front-ends, all through the single ForecastEx subsidiary. CME, CBOE and ICE each sit on both prediction-market-venue and clearing-and-collateral because in this architecture the venue and the clearing house are normally the same corporate family. The genuinely single-link listed names on this chain are NDAQ, GENI, KAMBI.ST, VIRT, HOOD, SCHW, PYPL, XYZ, PSFE and CRCL.

Venue rule, applied at a cost, twice. The most quotable numbers available for this chain are issuer-level: a listed brokerage's quarterly event-contract revenue line, and a listed sportsbook's annualised prediction-market trading volume disclosed in June 2026. Both are fundamentals figures for a named ticker, so under CLAUDE.md they resolve to data/market and data/edgar or they are NULL, and neither is carried here. The consequence is that this map's sizing is industry-level (AGA for the wagering pool, the CFTC rulemaking for event-contract notional) and no link carries a per-issuer economic. That is the correct trade at the chain stage and it is stated so the screen does not mistake the absence for a search that was never run.

Why the non-US ticker share is 1 of 26 and why that is not an oversight. The seed corpus runs 20 to 80 percent non-US because those chains are physical and their gating suppliers are Japanese, German, Chinese or Swedish. This one is a fight about US law, so the venues, the regulators and the demand are all American by construction. The map is still global by OWNERSHIP and the suffix count hides it: Sportradar is Swiss, Genius Sports is Guernsey-registered and British-run, Flutter is Irish and Paysafe is Bermudan, and all four chose US listings, so they read as US tickers to the calibrator. The single suffixed name, KAMBI.ST, sits on the state-regime branch, which is the branch where non-US B2B suppliers actually compete. If the Supreme Court takes the case and the state and tribal regime prevails, the non-US share of this map goes UP, because Playtech, Bragg and the rest of the European sportsbook-platform layer is the plumbing that outcome commissions.
